# Manual code review of apps/metis, round 1 (9 Oct 2026)

Shared brief for the six pdev reviewer agents dispatched by hand (not through plan-audit).
Each agent got this text verbatim plus its own scope section (listed at the end).

## Mode

This is NOT a plan-audit round. The owner asked for a manual review of the app that was just built,
`apps/metis` (repo root `/Users/mrpo/Documents/projects/metis`). There is no ticket plan to audit: your
artifacts are the source files in your scope. There is no kit report and no gate report to build on,
except `apps/metis/reports/verify.md`, which says every gate of `pnpm verify` was green (2,639 Jest tests,
coverage 100%, Stryker mutation score 100%, 108 Playwright tests). Do not re-report "gates are green";
attack what those gates cannot see.

Review focus set by the owner: code best practice, architecture, test suite.

## The owner's words

"I just did a quick review and already saw a lot of manual text hard-coded, scattered and even duplicated everywhere
in the app and the test suite, such as 'Northwind Furniture Co.', 'Client Delivery', not to mention that the
project even uses comments in Vietnamese."

Translation: "Skimming it I already saw a lot of hand-typed text hard-coded and scattered, even
duplicated, all over the app and the test suite, like 'Northwind Furniture Co.' and 'Client Delivery',
not to mention the project even uses comments in Vietnamese."

Treat both as confirmed symptoms. Your job: find the generative mechanism, size it, and find what ELSE
the same mechanism broke.

## App context

- Expo app (React Native + react-native-web, expo-router) for "Metis", a portfolio governance product.
  Built so far: the app shell (sidebar, rail, drawer, top bar, project header), screen 24 "Project
  overview" (`src/screens/24-project-overview/`), a design system (`src/design-system/`), English and
  Vietnamese UI copy, an MSW mock server and fixtures (`src/mocks/`), placeholder routes for screens not
  built yet (`src/app/`).
- Approved spec (Vietnamese): `spec/2026-10-05-frontend-foundation-spec.md`. Section 3 (lines 85 to 173)
  is the architecture: folder layout 3.1 (line 87), import boundaries enforced by ESLint 3.2 (line 111),
  data flow 3.3, mock server 3.4. Section 5.5 (line 305) is the translation layer. Section 9 (line 411)
  is the test system and the leanness rule; section 10 (line 455) the canaries.
- As-built plans: `plan/2026-10-05-frontend-foundation.md`, `plan/2026-10-06-frontend-overview-screen.md`
  (919 KB: never read it whole, grep it), `plan/2026-10-09-frontend-narrow-widths.md`,
  `plan/2026-10-09-frontend-trace-and-gaps.md`. The code was produced by agents that copied code blocks
  out of these Vietnamese plans: the likely origin of the Vietnamese comments and the restated literals.
- Next: plan C adds more screens, and a team of about 40 developers at an agency will extend this code.
  Judge every pattern by what happens when it is copied into 50 more screens.
- Gates (`apps/metis/scripts/verify.mjs`): ESLint (two custom rules in `eslint-rules/`), TypeScript, Jest
  with 100% coverage thresholds, Stryker mutation, Playwright on Chromium and WebKit, knip (dead code),
  a license check, a trace gate (`scripts/check-trace.mjs`), canaries (`scripts/canary.mjs`), a web
  release check (`scripts/check-web-release.mjs`).
- Size (non-test / test lines): src/app 181 / 0, src/core 494 / 938, src/platform 115 / 249, src/mocks
  387 / 144, src/design-system 1,932 / 2,544, src/shell 1,542 / 2,417, src/screens 1,476 / 2,668, e2e 230
  / 1,270, scripts 672 / 860, eslint-rules 155 / 202, root config files 611.

## What to look for, beyond your own profile checklist

A. Hard-coded literals and duplicated sources of truth: user-facing text in production code outside
   the dictionaries (accessibility labels, fallbacks, error text); fixture values restated as literals in
   unit tests, e2e specs and scripts instead of imported from or derived from the fixture module; the
   same literal (display names, ids, route paths, counts, labels, magic numbers, pixel sizes, colors,
   timeouts) defined in more than one place. For each pattern: name the single source of truth it
   should come from and the smallest mechanism that keeps it there.
B. Language of the code: Vietnamese comments, test titles (`describe`, `it`, `test`), error and log
   messages, script output, lint rule messages. Classify with counts per class. Recommend the convention
   (default unless you find a reason against it: English for code, comments, test titles and tool
   output; Vietnamese only in `strings/vi.ts` and in test data that exercises the vi locale) and the
   cheapest guard that keeps it that way (for example an ESLint rule or a gate check that rejects
   Vietnamese diacritics outside an allowlist). Also judge the comments that cite plan ruling ids: they
   point at Vietnamese plan files the agency will not read; say what such a comment should say instead
   (the why, in one English line) or whether it should go.
C. Everything else in your own dimension (your agent profile's checklist), applied to existing code
   instead of a plan.

## Rules for this run

- AGENT CORE RULES (verbatim from pdev `shared/digests/core.md`):
  1. Ground every claim in an artifact you actually opened - cite file:line. A claim about code, a
     token, a selector or a doc you did not read is invalid.
  2. Verdict cells hold MEASUREMENTS, never inferences: every PASS/FAIL carries `probe: <oracle +
     number>`. "The rule should not apply here" is not a verdict.
  3. Report `NOT RUN + reason` instead of silently skipping any mandated check; a missing dependency is
     reported, never replaced by a fallback.
  4. Never fabricate data (URLs, ids, copy, numbers): enumerate from an authoritative source or mark
     unknown.
  5. Platform claims carry `[Source: <reference>]` or `[Unverified - confirm before applying]`; a claim
     about platform behavior must include a citation and there is no third option.
  6. A finding names its file:line, says whether it is approach-changing, and proposes the smallest fix.
- Read-only. Edit nothing in the repo except your own findings file. Never run git add, commit or push.
- A Stryker mutation run from another session is using 5 cores on this machine right now (in
  `~/metis-run/verify`). Do NOT run Jest, Stryker, Playwright, tsc, ESLint, pnpm, npx or expo commands.
  Static review only: Read, Grep, Glob, and light shell (grep, wc, sed -n, python3 for counting). If a
  claim needs a run to prove, give the exact command and mark it `NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress`.
- Shell traps on this machine: a hook rewrites some commands. `rg` is not on PATH (use the Grep tool or
  `grep -rn`). A plain `find` with no match prints a summary line, so use `rtk proxy find`. Use `cmp` or
  `diff -u`, never a bare `diff`. If a grep summary looks odd ("N matches in 0 files"), rerun it as
  `rtk proxy grep ...`. In zsh a bare word starting with `=` is expanded, so quote separators. Each Bash
  call is a fresh shell: start it with `cd /Users/mrpo/Documents/projects/metis/apps/metis`.
- One finding per PATTERN, not per file: enumerate every occurrence with a count, the file list (or the
  exact command that reproduces it) and two or three representative file:line examples. Rank by impact;
  at most 25 findings.
- Severity in this code review: 🔴 blocker = a live defect in shipped behaviour (wrong output, crash,
  security), a test or gate that passes while the thing it guards is broken, or a systemic pattern every
  new screen will copy and that gets expensive to unwind (state the multiplier). 🟡 major = should be
  fixed before plan C builds more screens. 💭 nit = polish. Blockers and majors carry the `trigger` and
  `guard-bypass` lines your profile requires.
- The `edits` block of your profile does not apply (there is no plan file to patch). A mechanical fix
  gives the exact code change with file:line in its `Fix` line; a fix that needs a new mechanism (a lint
  rule, a shared builder, a gate) carries `- design: yes, <what is missing>`.
- Write in English. No em dashes or en dashes anywhere.
- Before your final reply, write your findings file at the path in your scope with one Bash heredoc
  (`cat > <path> <<'EOF'` with the quoted delimiter, so backticks and dollar signs survive), shaped
  exactly as your profile's Output section: first line `mode achieved: ...`, then the findings, then
  `OPENED: ...`. Then return the same content in your reply. Write the file by turn 25 at the latest; a
  partial report is never lost.
